snapshot.title: Time Jump: 10:00 AM — Emergency Activation

fields.narration: Facilitator: It is now 10:00 AM. The situation has escalated. The lab cannot process new samples. Customer service is operating on paper forms. The AMI outage map remains down. The public alert system is unable to issue any notices. The control network remains isolated from the business LAN. Telemetry from RTU-03 to RTU-07 is still unresponsive. The Mayor has contacted the City Manager to confirm whether the water is safe to drink. The Public Information Officer cannot draft a public advisory. The time has come to act. The Incident Commander must now declare a Level 3 emergency and activate the Incident Command System under the Emergency Response Plan.
worldState: The lab cannot process new samples. Paper forms are in use.
Customer service is operating on paper intake forms and printed critical-customer list. MBW-CIS-01 and the customer portal are unavailable.
The AMI outage map remains down; no new data since 09:00.
Telemetry from RTU-03 to RTU-07 remains unresponsive.
The Public Information Officer cannot draft a public advisory due to system unavailability.
The City Manager has been informed by the Mayor that the public is demanding confirmation on water safety.
The Incident Command System is now activated under ERP Section 4.
The Incident Commander has the authority to appoint ICS roles per C2, Section 3.
fields.facilitatorNote: This is a forced activation of ICS. The Incident Commander must now appoint the ICS roles from C2, Section 3. Watch for whether the IC declares a Level 3 emergency and correctly assigns the Technical Specialist, Water Quality Manager, and Public Information Officer.
